clips.text: Three weeks in: good morning texts, surprise gifts, "I've never felt this way about anyone."
It feels like a fairy tale. That's the point. Love bombing.
Affection this fast, before trust has had time to exist.
Then you set one boundary. You're busy Friday.
And the warmth vanishes. Short replies. No calls. Nothing.
The affection wasn't about you. It was about access.
Real interest survives a no. Love bombing punishes it.
Next time the warmth drops after a boundary, don't chase it. Name it.
Have you seen this switch? Tell me below.
"I never said that. You're remembering it wrong."
You heard it clearly. But they say it so calmly, you start checking yourself.
That's gaslighting. Deny what happened, then make your memory the problem.
One argument is a disagreement. A pattern of rewrites is control.
So write it down. The date, the words, what happened.
Paper doesn't get confused. Trust the record, not the rewrite.
When did you first notice the story changing? Tell me below.
You raise one thing that hurt you. Watch what happens next.
First, they deny it. "That didn't happen."
Then they attack. "You're always criticizing me."
Then the reversal. Suddenly they're the victim, and you're the one apologizing.
That's DARVO. Deny, attack, reverse victim and offender.
The conversation about their behavior just became a trial about yours.
Don't follow the reversal. Repeat the original point once, then stop.
Ever raised one concern and ended up apologizing? Tell me below.
After the argument, nothing. Days of no reply. Read, ignored.
No explanation. No return time. Just coldness, until you apologize.
That's the silent treatment. Withdrawal used as punishment, not space.
Real space sounds like this: "I need an hour. I'll come back and we'll talk."
Silence trains you to agree faster, bring up less, shrink.
Space has a return time. Punishment doesn't.
Ask once for a return time. If none comes, stop chasing the reply.
Which one have you lived with, space or silence? Tell me below.
You did exactly what they asked. The apology, the way they wanted it.
And suddenly, it's not enough. Now it's something else. Now it "doesn't count."
That's moving the goalposts. The standard changes every time you meet it.
The target moves each time you reach it, so you can never arrive.
That's not high standards. That's a game you can't win.
Next time, ask for the standard in writing. One clear ask, one clear done.
If it moves again, you have your answer.
Has this happened to you? Tell me below.
